partial_case.facts: The resident lives in a 2-bedroom house with her husband and young children. The landlord is aware she has respiratory health conditions. She reported flooring repairs and damp and mould affecting her living room in July 2023. On 4 July 2023, the resident told the landlord that the floorboards in her living room were damaged and her son had tripped and injured his head due to this. On 17 August 2023, the resident complained about the landlord's response to the flooring repair work, stating she was unhappy that it had not completed work, its operative attending on 14 July 2023 did not make the area safe but instead moved a toy box over the hole in the floor and left, the damaged floor was a safety hazard, there was mould in the living room and the floor was rotten, the landlord's communication was poor, and her son had been injured due to the damaged floor.

key_reasoning_quotes.text: The landlord did not carry out repair work to the floor in line with its policy timeframes and its communication around the issue was poor. Although it has apologised, it has not provided appropriate remedy to recognise the detriment caused to the resident.

The landlord failed to demonstrate that it responded to reports of damp and mould in line with its policies. It failed to address the issue in its complaint responses which meant it was unable to offer a sufficient resolution for the resident regarding the matter.

There were significant delays by the landlord in its handling of the complaint. Its communication with the resident was poor and it failed to provide appropriate remedy to recognise the impact this caused to her.

partial_case.facts: The resident lived in a 2-bedroom house with her husband and young children; the landlord knew she had respiratory health conditions, and she reported flooring repairs and damp and mould affecting the living room in July 2023. On 4 July 2023 the resident told the landlord the living-room floorboards were damaged and said her son had tripped and injured his head. On 17 August 2023 the resident complained about the landlord’s response to the flooring repair work, saying work had not been completed, the area had not been made safe, there was mould in the living room, communication was poor, and her son had been injured due to the damaged floor. On 19 September 2023 the landlord’s stage 1 response said it had completed repair work to the floor on 21 July 2023 and asked the resident to forward evidence if she disputed this. On 20 September 2023 the resident escalated the complaint to stage 2 and repeated that the floor repair work was outstanding. Between November 2023 and February 2024 the resident chased the landlord for its stage 2 response, saying the floor remained damaged, damp and mould had not been addressed, her health was affected, personal items had been damaged, and vermin had been attracted. On 23 February 2024 the landlord sent its stage 2 response, apologised for delay and distress, said there had been service failure in its handling of the repair work, said it completed floor repair work on 23 February 2024, and provided a compensation claim form for injury and damaged items. The resident remained dissatisfied with the final response and brought the complaint to the Ombudsman, saying the landlord had failed to respond adequately and had not offered compensation.

Maladministration in the landlord’s handling of reports of damp and mould

The landlord provided its stage 2 response 106 working days after acknowledging the resident’s escalation request, following our intervention. This is significantly longer than the timescales set out in its policy.
